findings.F1: Inside the choppy-calm profile, on the 7-day grid of folds B and C, the forward excess return rises with the swing-scaled 14-day move (slope 0.042, day-clustered t 2.69, 151 cases on 65 days; on the forecast 0.0023, t 2.02). Step 5's slope over all four folds is 0.00027 with t 0.35 on 777 cases. The effect seen in B and C therefore barely survives in folds A and D. The full test's result is on the predicted side but close to zero.
findings.F2: The test already used every fold and every coin on daily bars. More 1d data is not available. A finer bar does not add independent 7-day cases either.
findings.F3: Inside the profile the carry is driven by the largest moves, and above all by the largest rises:
findings.F4: The falling side does not carry in a graded way:
findings.F5: The effect is uneven in time. Only 2021 is clearly positive (+5.4 % per case, t 2.77, n 51). Window w18 alone gives +15.9 % (t 3.41, n 13). 2019 is -0.1 % (t -0.06), and w7/w8 are slightly negative. This explains why the effect drowns in the folds not shown.
findings.F6: The horizon is not the cause:
findings.F7: Outside the profile the carry is weaker per unit of move than inside (clustered slope 0.0128, t 1.39, 994 cases, against 0.042 inside). It is still graded across |z| quartiles, from +1.0 % to +2.8 % (top quartile t 2.45). The choppy-calm profile concentrates the effect but is not its only home.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, a coin whose 14-day rise, measured against its own daily swing over the past 30 days, is large keeps rising over the next 7 days, and the larger that swing-scaled rise, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: In choppy calm markets a trader can buy coins after unusually large swing-scaled 14-day rises, sized by the rise. Following swing-scaled falls short has no support.
ideas.name: choppy calm large rises carry
